title: Derivatives
source: Stewart, Calculus 8e; additions from Dawkins Calc II/III notes

children.title: Why is the derivative the slope you see when you zoom in?
children.summary: Zooms into a smooth curve until it looks straight; that straight line's slope is f′(a) (spec below)
children.spec: Zoom: a microscope on y = x² at a = 1; each ×10 zoom makes the curve straighter. Read: the zoomed line's slope is measured live and converges to 2. Corner: the same microscope on |x| at 0 never straightens. Link: the difference-quotient secant overlaid, with h tied to the zoom level.

children.title: Why is a derivative a rate of change?
children.summary: Compares the odometer (position) with the speedometer (its derivative), driven live

children.title: Why has |x| no derivative at 0?
children.summary: Zooms in forever and the corner never straightens

children.title: Why does differentiable imply continuous, but not conversely?
children.summary: Sees a jump kill the derivative, while a corner is continuous but still not differentiable

children.title: Draw f′ from f
children.summary: Slides a slope-meter along f and plots the readings to build f′

children.title: Derivative from the definition
children.summary: Simplifies the difference quotient, then lets h → 0

children.title: How tangents were found before calculus
children.summary: Tries Fermat's and Barrow's methods on a parabola

children.title: Why is d/dx xⁿ = nxⁿ⁻¹?
children.summary: Grows a square of side x by dx: the new area is about 2x·dx; a cube grows on 3 faces, giving 3x²·dx

children.title: Why the product rule?
children.summary: Grows a u × v rectangle: two thin strips u·dv + v·du, plus a corner too small to count

children.title: Why the quotient rule?
children.summary: Builds it from the product rule applied to u = (u/v)·v

children.title: Why is eˣ its own derivative?
children.summary: Tries bases 2, 2.5, 3 and finds the one whose slope at 0 is exactly 1

children.title: Rule drill
children.summary: Picks the right rule for random functions

children.title: Second derivatives and the equations they satisfy
children.summary: Differentiates y = A cos x + B sin x twice and checks y″ + y = 0

children.title: Build a better roller coaster
children.summary: Joins track pieces so the heights and slopes match and the ride is smooth

children.title: Why does sin θ / θ → 1, and only in radians?
children.summary: Squeezes the sector between two triangles; switching to degrees makes the limit π/180

children.title: Why is (sin x)′ = cos x?
children.summary: Runs a point on the unit circle: its vertical speed is its horizontal position

children.title: Why is (cos x)′ = −sin x?
children.summary: Uses the same circle: the horizontal speed is minus the height

children.title: Derivatives of tan, sec, csc, cot
children.summary: Derives each from sin and cos with the quotient rule

children.title: Why do rates multiply?
children.summary: Turns three gears: if A turns 3 times as fast as B, and B twice as fast as C, then A turns 6 times as fast as C

children.title: Why do you need the inside derivative?
children.summary: Squeezes sin(2x) and watches its slopes double

children.title: Peel the onion
children.summary: Differentiates nested functions layer by layer

children.title: Where should a pilot start descent?
children.summary: Fits a smooth cubic glide path that meets the runway level

children.title: How can a curve that isn't a function have a slope?
children.summary: Finds tangents all around the circle x² + y² = 25

children.title: Why is dy/dx = −x/y on a circle?
children.summary: Sees the tangent is perpendicular to the radius

children.title: Implicit stepper
children.summary: Differentiates both sides, treating y as y(x)

children.title: Families of implicit curves
children.summary: Changes a parameter and watches the curve family morph

children.title: Why is an inverse function's slope the reciprocal?
children.summary: Reflects a tangent line in y = x: rise and run swap

children.title: Why is (ln x)′ = 1/x?
children.summary: Reads it as the reciprocal of eˣ's slope at the mirrored point

children.title: Why is (aˣ)′ = aˣ ln a?
children.summary: Rewrites aˣ as e^(x ln a); ln a is the stretch

children.title: Why does logarithmic differentiation tame xˣ?
children.summary: Takes ln first so the exponent comes down

children.title: Why is (arctan x)′ = 1/(1 + x²)?
children.summary: Reads it off the triangle with tan θ = x

children.title: Derivatives of sinh and cosh
children.summary: Sees them behave like sin and cos with one sign flipped (see Exponentials & Logarithms → Hyperbolic Functions)

children.title: Derivative table quiz
children.summary: Practises the exp, log, inverse-trig and hyperbolic derivatives

children.title: Why is velocity the derivative of position, and acceleration of velocity?
children.summary: Sees three linked graphs (s, v, a) updating together

children.title: Why does a sliding ladder's top speed up near the ground?
children.summary: Pulls the foot out at a steady speed; the top's speed blows up as it nears the ground

children.title: Why does a balloon's radius grow more slowly as it inflates?
children.summary: Pumps in air at a constant rate; the same volume spreads over a bigger surface

children.title: Related-rates stepper
children.summary: Writes the relation, differentiates in t, then substitutes

children.title: Rates across the sciences
children.summary: Sees current = dQ/dt, reaction rates, marginal cost and population growth as one idea

children.title: Filling a cone with water
children.summary: Sees the water level rise fast first, then slow

children.title: Why is the tangent the best straight-line guess?
children.summary: Compares lines through the point; only the tangent's error shrinks faster than the distance

children.title: Why is √4.1 ≈ 2.025?
children.summary: Rides the tangent at x = 4 instead of the curve (true value 2.0248…)

children.title: Why is sin x ≈ x for small x?
children.summary: Zooms in at 0 until the two graphs merge; this is why the pendulum formula works

children.title: dy versus Δy
children.summary: Sees the tangent's rise against the curve's rise

children.title: Measurement error
children.summary: Measures a radius as 21 ± 0.05 cm and estimates the error in the volume

children.title: Taylor polynomials, a first look
children.summary: Adds a quadratic term to beat the tangent line

children.title: Why is dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt)?
children.summary: Runs a point along the curve; over a tiny time step the rise and run are y′dt and x′dt, so the dt cancels (spec below)
children.spec: Motion: a point runs along x = t² − 3t, y = t³ − 3t with velocity arrows x′(t) and y′(t) drawn. Tiny step: zoom on one time step dt; the little run is x′dt, the rise y′dt, and the slope ratio cancels dt. Special tangents: scrub t to find where x′ = 0 (vertical) and y′ = 0 (horizontal); both cases are highlighted live. Second derivative: the common trap y″/x″ is shown failing against the correct d/dt(dy/dx) ÷ x′.

children.title: Horizontal and vertical tangents
children.summary: Sees dy/dt = 0 flatten the tangent and dx/dt = 0 stand it up

children.title: How can one point have two tangents?
children.summary: Watches a self-crossing curve pass the same point twice with two different slopes

children.title: Why isn't d²y/dx² = y″(t)/x″(t)?
children.summary: Differentiates dy/dx with respect to t, then divides by dx/dt, and compares it with the wrong guess

children.title: Slopes of polar curves
children.summary: Writes x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ and applies the parametric rule

children.title: Why does a cycloid have cusps?
children.summary: Sees the rolling point stop dead (x′ = y′ = 0) every time it touches the ground
